values: Canonical examples selected for the first learning units. Teaching status is separate from source approval.
Starter assets for action-first syntax, commands, tense, aspect, questions, negation, address, practical repair, and a first conditional.
Baseline sentence for recognizing and arranging VSO order.
The subject is understood rather than spoken.
Adds a clear object and inclusive first-person plural subject.
Past tense attaches to the verb.
I will go to the water.
Future tense attaches to the verb.
I am going to the water.
Continuous aspect follows the verb as a suffix.
I have gone to the water.
Perfective aspect presents the action as completed.
I usually go to the water.
Habitual aspect marks a usual or repeated action.
I do not go to the water.
Ver sits directly before the verb.
Do you go to the water?
Ra frames the sentence as a question.
Will you go to the water in the city?
Combines future time with an explicit spatial setting.
I go to the water, friend.
Plain role address creates a casual or familiar tone.
I go to the water, respected friend.
Li- marks respect on the form of address.
Respected one, please go to the water.
Combines direct command structure with respectful address.
I go to the water at dawn.
Adds a time-of-day setting to the baseline movement sentence.
I drink the water at noon.
A second action pattern prevents overlearning only Var sentences.
Useful command for removing ambiguity from what was said.
Practical command using an approved boundary-crossing verb.
Rath Ya var dren, Nor-var I shena.
If you go to the water, I will bring coinage.
First multi-clause asset in the starter pack.

values: Draft app exercises derived from the canonical Sentence Bank. Review each prompt and accepted answer before approval.
Var is the movement action, so it comes first.
Put the sentence in Celan order: I go to the water.
Celan normally begins with the action.
The action Var comes before the subject I and destination dren.
Use the sentence translation as context.
Var carries the core action of going or moving.
Which word marks this as a command?
Va tells the listener that the clause is an instruction.
Build the command: Go to the water!
Va comes first, followed by the action var and destination dren.
Build the sentence: We eat the bread.
Velaen is the verb, Ilin the subject, and morlak the object.
Find the participant after the verb.
Ilin is the inclusive we that performs the action.
Change Var I dren. into the past.
Past time is marked before the verb.
Tha- attaches to var to place the movement in the past.
Change Var I dren. into the future.
Future time is marked before the verb.
Nor- attaches to var to place the movement in the future.
Choose the form meaning I am going to the water.
Varal I dren.; Varath I dren.; Varas I dren.
The -al suffix marks the movement as ongoing.
Choose the form meaning I have gone to the water.
Varal I dren.; Varath I dren.; Varas I dren.
The -ath suffix presents the movement as completed.
Choose the form meaning I usually go to the water.
Varal I dren.; Varath I dren.; Varas I dren.
The -as suffix marks a usual or repeated action.
Place the negative marker directly before the verb.
Ver sits immediately before var while VSO order remains intact.
The marker comes directly before the verb.
Build the question: Do you go to the water?
Ra comes first, followed by the normal verb-subject-destination order.
Questions announce themselves at the beginning.
Ra frames the entire clause as a question.
Build the future question: Will you go to the water in the city?
Keep the future verb first, then subject and destination.
Nor-var carries future movement. The city phrase follows the destination.
Choose the casual form of address.
Var I dren, Ser.; Var I dren, Li-Ser.
The casual form has no honorific prefix.
Ser is the plain familiar address. Li-Ser adds respect.
Choose the respectful form of address.
Var I dren, Ser.; Var I dren, Li-Ser.
Li- marks the addressed friend as respected.
Build the respectful command: Respected one, please go to the water.
Address the person, then give the command.
Li-Ya supplies respectful address. Va then marks the command.
Build the sentence: I go to the water at dawn.
Begin with the action and place the time setting last.
The VSO core stays together before the dawn setting.
Which words give the time setting?
Find the part that means at dawn.
An Kinnshal supplies the time-of-day setting in this established example.
Build the sentence: I drink the water at noon.
Put the action before the subject.
Tal is the action in this established sentence, followed by I and dren.
Look at the first word in the Celan sentence.
Tal carries the drinking action in this established example.
Build the repair sentence: I do not understand.
Put the negative marker before the comprehension verb.
Ver negates nemaen, and the subject follows the verb.
Build the request: Clarify what was said.
Va marks the request, followed by the action, listener, and object.
Build the command: Come inside the room.
Start with Va and keep the action before the listener.
The command uses the approved boundary-crossing verb anshanaen.
Which word makes this a command?
Va marks the clause as an instruction.
Build the conditional: If you go to the water, I will bring coinage.
Nor-var I shena; Rath; Ya var dren
Rath Ya var dren, Nor-var I shena.
rath Ya var dren, nor-var I shena.
Begin the condition with Rath, then give the future result.
Rath opens the condition. The second clause carries the future result.
The conditional marker begins the first clause.
Rath means if and introduces the condition.

values: These objectives connect the sentence assets and exercises to one staged Celan curriculum.
Identify the verb or action in a short Celan sentence.
Place the action before the subject and object or destination.
Recognize Var as the core movement action in the baseline sentence.
Place Va at the beginning of a command and preserve action-first order.
Attach Tha- to the verb to place an action in the past.
Attach Nor- to the verb to place an action in the future.
Distinguish continuous, perfective, and habitual action.
Place Ver directly before the verb or verbal form being negated.
Place Ra at the beginning of a direct question.
Distinguish casual address from respectful Li- address.
Keep the core sentence intact while adding an approved time or place setting.
Say that understanding is absent and ask another speaker to clarify.
Introduce an if-clause with Rath and connect it to a result clause.
